headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error risks: Rasa can transmit conversation data to allowlisted channels while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge source with no isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between awesome-selfhosted and Rasa, so prompt injection is not default. However, Rasa ingests text/voice from external channels and can be influenced by user-controlled content; if awesome-selfhosted content is manually copied into those channels, injection becomes possible. The pairwise pathway is indirect and low blast radius.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted content is manually pasted into a Rasa channel message
IF Rasa treats incoming channel text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Restrict copy-paste of repository text into bot conversations
Add a prompt-injection filter on inbound messages
Use a separate review queue for pasted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa has allowlisted network egress and multiple external API surfaces, so conversation data can leave the local environment by default. awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management source with no declared data classes, but if it is used to curate sensitive notes or links, those contents can flow into Rasa outputs or channels. The interaction is plausible in default deployments and can expose multiple work products.
conditions: IF sensitive notes from awesome-selfhosted are copied into Rasa conversation state
IF Rasa forwards conversation content to any listed external channel
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive content in shared notes
Disable unnecessary channel integrations
Review outbound message templates for embedded user text
Limit retention of conversation transcripts
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Rasa supports multiple external channels but no shared filesystem or overlapping write scope is documented here. The pair therefore has no meaningful default write conflict; only a narrow operational overlap exists through external messaging channels.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same external workspace or channel
IF an operator adds shared mutable storage outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid shared writable directories
Document ownership of each external channel
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can act on dialogue inputs and route them through channel integrations, while awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge source that may be treated as authoritative by an operator. If content from awesome-selfhosted is copied into Rasa without verification, Rasa can propagate incorrect or stale recommendations to users. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF content from awesome-selfhosted is used as source material for Rasa responses
IF no human verification step checks the copied guidance before sending
mitigations: Require human review before publishing recommendations
Add source/date labels to imported guidance
Use a checklist for factual verification
Limit Rasa to templated responses for curated content
requires-engineering: add citation-aware response gating

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is limited. Rasa handles text and voice and can send data through external channels, while awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge list with no declared sensitive-data handling. The pair only raises compliance concerns if regulated data is introduced into Rasa workflows.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Rasa conversations
IF outbound channel integrations transmit that regulated data to third parties
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the bot
Disable unnecessary third-party channels
Add a data-classification banner for operators
Review retention settings for transcripts
requires-engineering: implement residency and DPA controls
